question: Does my insurance change after my visa switches from D-4 to D-2?
required_facts: As an ERICA degree (D-2) student you get the university group insurance, KRW 25,000 per semester billed with tuition
National Health Insurance also applies to international students (monthly bill)
While in the language course, insurance questions go to the language school
reference_answer: Yes. While you are a language-course (D-4) student, insurance questions go to your language school. Once you start a degree on D-2 at ERICA, your insurance is the university group insurance (KRW 25,000 per semester, charged on your tuition bill) plus National Health Insurance, which NHIS bills monthly.
notes: Campus from persona (ERICA); the question does not state it. Seoul degree students would instead get university-paid private insurance (47317421).

question: Can I work part time here?
required_facts: Need a part-time work permit with confirmation from the university's international-student officer
D-2-8 visiting/exchange students: 6 months must have passed since entry
GPA of at least 2.0 last semester and the Korean (or, for English track, English) proficiency standard
Allowed hours depend on degree level, year and language level
reference_answer: Possibly. Clarifying question: 'Which visa do you hold (for example D-2 or D-2-8) and what program are you in?' For a D-2-8 exchange student: you need a part-time permit confirmed by the international-student officer, 6 months must have passed since your entry, your last-semester GPA must be at least 2.0, and English-track students can meet the language rule with TOEFL 530/iBT 71 or IELTS 5.5.
notes: Hard: many unstated attributes; visa splits most (D-2-8 6-month rule). Hours for non-degree exchange students are not in the table. Seoul confirmation form (45669e0e, 2025-10) gives 20/25/30 hours, conflicting with the ERICA table (10/30, 15/35) - needs adjudication.

question: Which insurance rules apply to me?
required_facts: ERICA: university group insurance KRW 25,000 per semester, charged on the tuition bill
Seoul: university private insurance paid by the university for enrolled students
Both: National Health Insurance, billed monthly by NHIS (79,320 won from March 2026)

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul private insurance; gold student is ERICA

reference_answer: At ERICA you have two policies: the university group insurance (KRW 25,000 per semester, charged with tuition) and National Health Insurance, which NHIS bills monthly to your ARC address (79,320 won from March 2026). At Seoul, the university pays the private insurance for enrolled students, and NHI applies the same way.
notes: Campus unstated; university insurance differs by campus. Exchange students are fee-waived, so how ERICA bills them is unclear (caveat).

The newest career event on the ERICA board open to graduates is the Hyundai E&C popup recruiting session, March 16-20, 2026
reference_answer: Of the graduate-focused events, the Global Career Start Online Program (posted 28 October 2025, international graduate students only, applications 20 October-17 November 2025) is newer than the 2025 Job Fair for Internationals (posted 10 September 2025). notes: Hard: 'which is newer' is ambiguous (posting date vs event date; which events compared). All listed events are past as of 2026-11.

question: Will immigration definitely approve my D-4 to D-2 change?
required_facts: Nobody can guarantee approval; immigration decides and may ask for more documents
D-4 to D-2 needs: application form, passport, ARC, photo, admission letter, tuition receipt, language-school attendance/transcript, proof of residence, KRW 130,000
If language-school attendance is below 70%: bank statement (KRW 10-20 million) and a statement
reference_answer: No one can promise approval; the immigration office decides and may ask for extra documents. For D-4 to D-2 you need the application form, passport, ARC, photo, standard admission letter, tuition receipt, language-school attendance certificate and transcripts, proof of residence and the KRW 130,000 fee; with attendance below 70% you also need a bank statement (KRW 10 million for the university's own language school) and a statement.
notes: Required fact 1 (certainty) has no span by nature; partial per 9.1.

question: Where do I check my result and what comes after that?
required_facts: Check the result on the admission result page ([Admission Information]); print the acceptance certificate and tuition bill
Pick the acceptance guideline by the 'Korean Language' result on that page
Pass/exempt: pay tuition 2026.06.18-07.09, bank balance certificate and CoA application by July 16, then D-2 visa
Fail: pay tuition, submit TOPIK 4 / IIE level 4 by July 16 or be placed on leave of absence (IIE/D-4 route)

inapplicable_evidence.why: Korean Standard Fail guide; gold profile is exempt

reference_answer: Check your result on the international admission results page under [Admission Information], where you also print the acceptance certificate and tuition bill. question: Can I still get a part-time permit?
required_facts: Yes, after 6 months have passed since entry (D-2-8 rule)
English-track students meet the language standard with TOEFL 530 / iBT 71, IELTS 5.5, CEFR 82 or TEPS 601+
Previous-semester GPA of at least 2.0 and the university officer's confirmation
reference_answer: Yes, without TOPIK: as an English-track student you meet the language rule with TOEFL 530 (iBT 71), IELTS 5.5, CEFR 82 or TEPS 601 or higher. As a D-2-8 student you can apply only once 6 months have passed since entry, your last-semester GPA must be at least 2.0, and the university's international-student officer must confirm the permit. With the standard met, year 3-4 students may work up to 30 hours on weekdays.
notes: Hours conflict: Seoul confirmation form (45669e0e, 2025-10) says 20 h/week for undergraduates (25 IEQAS) vs ERICA table 30 h; hours kept out of required facts.

question: When should I start the D-10 change?
required_facts: D-10-1 eligibility: legally staying in Korea with a bachelor's degree or higher and enough points (or the Korean-university-graduate exemption)
Your D-2 ends with graduation, so the change must be made while you still stay legally
The exact time window for applying is not stated
reference_answer: The D-10-1 job-seeker visa is for people legally staying in Korea who hold at least a bachelor's degree and pass the points test (graduates of Korean universities within 3 years with TOPIK 4 are exempt), and a D-2 ends with graduation, so apply after your degree is conferred while your stay is still legal. The pages do not give an exact application window, so confirm the timing with the ERICA OIA or immigration (1345).
notes: Timing not stated anywhere; partial per 9.1.
